abstract: Let $X$ be a projective hyper-Kähler fourfold of $K3^{[2]}$-type whose transcendental Hodge structure has endomorphism field $\mathbb Q$, and let $\Sigma\subset X$ be a smooth K3 surface on which the symplectic form does not vanish. Restriction to $\Sigma$ multiplies the Beauville–Bogomolov form on $T(X)$ by a positive rational number $c$, the multiplier of $\Sigma$, which is an integer when $\rho(X)\le2$. When $T(X)$ is the transcendental lattice of a K3 surface $S$, a non-square multiplier gives an algebraic Hodge similarity $T(S)_{\mathbb Q}\to T(\Sigma)_{\mathbb Q}$ that is not a scaled isometry, and the Hodge conjecture for $S\times\Sigma$. Generalized Nikulin surfaces give $c=2$ on families of dimension $12$. We show that this mechanism gives only squares at small Picard number. If $\rho(X)=1$, then $X$ contains no smooth K3 surface. If $\rho(X)=2$, then $c\in\{1,4,16\}$. For Hilbert squares $S^{[2]}$ with $\rho(S)=1$, $c=4$. The proofs combine the self-intersection formula $[\Sigma]^2=\int_\Sigma c_2(X)-24$ with Fujiki's relations, an explicit description of $H^4(X,\mathbb Z)$, a determinant identity for the restricted Néron–Severi form, and one positivity condition: the restricted form minus $c$ times the Beauville–Bogomolov form is non-negative on nef classes. The cohomological conditions alone leave $c=19$ on moduli spaces $M_S(2,h,28)$ over K3 surfaces of degree $114$. There we construct an integral Hodge class and a K3 surface of degree $6$ that satisfy all of them. The positivity condition, with the Bayer–Macrì description of nef cones, excludes this case. For immersed surfaces with double points the bound on $c$ disappears.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: Version 2 addresses the review of version 1. (1) Attribution: a remark after Lemma 5.1 cites hodge_conjecture_80/v2, Lemma 3.1, where the Wirtinger inequality already gives $M(k)\ge c\,q(k)$ for Kähler $k$, and explains that the proof here instead deforms $k$ by a $(1,1)$-class in $T$ and uses that $j^*T$ and $j^*N$ are orthogonal. A remark before Corollary 3.3 places Proposition 3.2 next to Qin–Wang and Kapfer. (2) Every "from memory" annotation is replaced by a precise reference: Torelli by [Markman, survey, Thm. 1.3(1)]; the monodromy group by [Markman, survey, Lemma 9.2]; Eichler's criterion, the splitting $T\cong U\oplus T'$, uniqueness in the genus and surjectivity of $O(L)\to O(A_L)$ by Huybrechts' K3 book, Ch. 14; smooth curves in $|e|$ by a base-point-freeness argument from the same book, Cor. 2.3.14. The local-freeness input for the $\mathbb P^1$-bundle in Proposition 5.4 is now explicit: $F_0$ is stable with $v(F_0)^2=-2$, so $\operatorname{ext}^1(F_0,F_0)=0$ by the twisted Mukai pairing [Bayer–Macrì, Def. 2.7]; a rigid stable sheaf of positive rank is locally free by Mukai's argument, which is local and so also applies on the twisted K3 surface. The uniqueness of $F_0$, which v1 quoted, is not used. The Eichler step now also passes from the $O(\Lambda)$-orbit to the $O^+(\Lambda)$-orbit, which v1 left implicit. (3) The introduction and abstract say that the multiplier $c$ is rational in general and an integer for $\rho(X)\le2$ (Lemma 3.4). (4) Proposition D calls its identities the specified necessary cohomological conditions, and names positivity as a further necessary condition. Remark 7.1 says only that without a bound on double points the equation has no uniform upper bound on $c$, which does not make large $c$ realizable. (5) Each sentence that cites a script now names the script that performs the check; `selfint_constraint.py` now also checks the Lagrangian plane. No new mathematical claims.
title: Multipliers of smooth K3 surfaces in hyper-Kähler fourfolds of K3^[2]-type
